proof_summary: If the relevant Fermat number is prime, its totient is exactly $2^{2^{33}}$, and the general bound $2^{2^{33}}\mid\varphi(m)\Rightarrow m\ge 2^{2^{33}}+1$ makes it minimal. Otherwise, even candidates satisfy $\varphi(m)\le m/2$, while any smaller odd candidate would have totient exactly $2^{2^{33}}$ and hence be squarefree with distinct Fermat-prime factors; uniqueness of binary expansion forces the sole factor to be the index-$33$ Fermat number, contradicting its nonprimality.
